responsibilities: Collaborate with engineers, analysts, and stakeholders to understand data needs and define clear analytics requirements.
Build, maintain, and troubleshoot data pipelines and transformations that produce reliable, analytics-ready data.
Develop and maintain data models, schemas, metric definitions, and documentation for reporting and analysis.
Implement data validation and quality checks, investigate anomalies, and communicate issues and recommended actions.
Integrate data from APIs, operational systems, data lakes, and data warehouses while maintaining appropriate data governance.
Monitor pipeline performance and reliability, participate in code reviews, and contribute to continuous process improvement.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Implement data validation and quality checks, investigate anomalies
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Validation, quality checks, governance, code reviews and reliability dominate; the single velocity phrase "fast-paced, startup-like environment" sits in the requirements.
evidence.domain_risk: advanced data analytics to support the warfighters and the intelligence community
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Defence sector, but the data is internal Engineering and Operations data and the responsibilities carry no financial or regulatory language, so moderate; the role is gated by "Active Secret clearance required.", which the schema has no field for.
evidence.collaboration_width: software engineers; analysts; Engineering; Operations; technical infrastructure teams
evidence.data_team_maturity: transitioning Engineering and Operations from legacy software and infrastructure to modern digital practices
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A named Digital Architecture Team has already built a microservices platform and is moving the business off legacy systems, so the data function exists and is growing.
evidence.jd_authorship: Collaborate with engineers, analysts, and stakeholders to understand data needs and define clear analytics requirements.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The six responsibility bullets are generic data-role tasks with no named tools, volumes or methods; the specifics sit in the intro and requirements.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: ensuring that data is collected, transformed, validated, documented, and made available for our end customers
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The audience is internal data consumers in Engineering and Operations, served through analytics-ready datasets.
evidence.autonomy_level: you will help turn that data into trusted, analytics-ready information
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Verbs are build, maintain, troubleshoot and "contribute to continuous process improvement", with escalation "when appropriate", so the role delivers scoped work.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tools or AI-facing data work are expected of the candidate.
evidence.testing_framing: Implement data validation and quality checks
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Validation and quality checks are a named responsibility the candidate implements.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The fear is pipeline reliability and data quality issues reaching customers, not compliance.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Build, maintain, and troubleshoot data pipelines and transformations
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The work is maintaining and troubleshooting pipelines while migrating off legacy infrastructure, so fix_scale.
evidence.loss_aversion: "Ability to monitor, troubleshoot, and communicate data quality or production issues, escalating when appropriate." frames reliability as an operational duty.
